I think these two phenomenons are somewhat related, and have been of importance to the social and political climate of the west for decades; they were significant with the latest US presidential election too:

 

The apparent exalted status of entertainers

Why would anyone assume that e.g. Lady Gaga or Jon Bon Jovi or Robert DeNiro have an authorative opinion on politics? Of course, this has been around at least as long as the Beatles, who allegedly managed to have segregation in the Southern states suspended in the ventures where they played in the 1960s. But how, when and why did entertainers become sages?

 

The challenging of authority

Both Brexit and the Trump victory are perceived by friend and foe as somehwat of an uprise against authority, while they might as well be described as a restoration of older, arguably more conservative, authority. Could it be that this is something ingrained in the Western (or maybe human) psyche? Why is it considered romantic to standup and rally, and boring to establish rules?
Two Psychosocial Phenomenons that warrant a closer examination

I think the first question has a lot to do with movement toward secularism.

Instead of gods, we've adopted human paragon worship. They age and die and get robbed like the rest of us, but that's irrelevant to their status. One might argue that religion, worship of the divine, instead of a crutch (which is what many atheists would call it), is in fact a cornerstone of psychosocial health.
